title: Hustling as assistant director: plugging songs for publishers
summary: Unpaid as assistant director, Thomas screens songwriters' material, gets ten dollars per radio play, and learns how plugging builds hits.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: I wasn't satisfied with that. That's when I started to hustling. I didn't know nothing about hustling. But Cab wasn't paying me extra money to be Assistant Director. It was just a title. So I got close to the songwriters. The songwriters would come, and he didn't have time for them. I'd take the song and I'd say, 'Well, let us play it for a couple of days, and I'll let you know if we can put it on the air.' So I'd pass it out and we'd play it. And I'd always check with Cab if he wanted to play it. Because it meant something for us to work with the publicists, you know. Because Mills was the one that got us there, and he was a stone publicist. And that's how I used to make... First I'd... Sometimes a guy would give me fifty dollars to make an arrangement, and if I couldn't get the fifty dollars to make arrangements... I worked out a deal every time I'd put it on the air, he'd give me ten dollars. So all I had to do was get it on five or six times. Sometimes I got it
on the air eight times; I'd make eighty dollars.
I got so close to the publicists, that when they'd come to the Cotton Club, they'd come to see me. They wouldn't see Cab. They'd try to see him if they could...
They used to give you all kinds of gifts, like pots and pans...

And I could go to any show that Chapelle(?) had. Leo Dixon was working for Chappelle(?)... I could get a ticket to any show that they had music on. I never paid to go see none of them shows. And I just got close to them, and I was their boy. And I found out if they got a song on the air five times during that night, they almost had a hit. They were the ones that I just learned if you play a song long enough, people will catch on to it.

And that's what they used to do. If they could get a song on... And sometimes, Leo and them would come and say, "Man, I need just one more play" -- and I'd sneak it in there. Because I used to have to make up the program.
